svg.text: Proactive splits in v1: at most one split per write, never a chain
A leaf needs a split when it has at most one free slot. Each internal node counts its children that need one (P) and keeps a free slot reserved for each:
needsSplit(internal) = (P == F). Before inserting, the write splits the deepest node on its path that needs a split. Same capacities as before: 4 children, 6 entries.
L2 has one free slot, so it needs a split; R reserves a slot for L2′
not full, but its only free slot is reserved
needs a split: one free slot
the deepest pending node on the path is the leaf L2 → split L2 first, then insert. R absorbs the sibling in its reserved slot: F−P unchanged, no cascade.
now physically full, same split state as before
L3 does not need a split; the deepest pending node on the path is R → split R by weight before inserting. A new root appears; no leaf splits.
1 split this write (R), then m goes into L3
L2′ reaches one free slot and starts needing a split. Only a counter moves: R′ reserves a slot (P=1 ≤ F=2), T is untouched. No split this write.
delta stops at R′: its split state did not change
0 splits this write; the next write into L2′ will split it, and R′ already has room
Splitting a pending child consumes one free parent slot and removes one pending child: F−P is unchanged, so the parent never needs to split
in the same write. Internal nodes split by weight (N + P), so both halves come out with P < F. A write therefore splits at most one existing node.
Split-state propagation stops at the first ancestor whose split state does not change; other metadata updates may continue upward.
